name: Payroll for restaurant chains
description: Dull as dishwater. Also: 40,000 restaurants would pay you every month without thinking about it.

name: Satellite photos for insurers
description: Insurers pay a fortune to see flood and fire risk from orbit. Slow to sell, enormous contracts.

name: Software for funeral homes
description: Nobody wants to build it. Everybody needs it. Customers never leave.

name: A better calendar
description: Everyone complains about calendars. Almost nobody switches.

name: Scheduling for hair salons
description: 200,000 salons, all using paper. Tiny payments, but they add up.

name: Fraud detection for small banks
description: Banks move slowly and pay enormously. You will spend two years in meetings.

name: An app that reads your medical letters
description: Turns doctor-speak into plain English. People love it. Regulators watch you.

name: Inventory software for hardware shops
description: Old customers, old computers, extremely loyal.

name: A search engine for legal documents
description: Lawyers bill by the hour and hate wasting it. They'll pay.

name: Translation for video games
description: Games need 20 languages on launch day. Rush jobs, good margins.

name: Software for beekeepers
description: There are more commercial beekeepers than you'd think. They're all on paper.

name: A tool that reads contracts for you
description: Flags the bad clauses. Terrifying if it's wrong.

name: Booking for tattoo artists
description: Artists hate admin. They will pay you to never do it again.

name: Website builder for churches
description: Half a million churches. Nobody is selling to them properly.

name: Sensors for old buildings
description: Tells you a wall is about to fail before it does. Cities buy slowly and forever.

name: A quieter air conditioner
description: Everyone hates the noise. Nobody has fixed it. Manufacturing will hurt.

name: Refill machines for supermarkets
description: Shoppers bring their own bottles. Supermarkets love the story, hate the mess.

name: Better bike locks
description: Thieves are extremely motivated. So are cyclists.

name: Charging points for rural roads
description: Nobody is building them. Somebody has to.

name: A vending machine for fresh bread
description: Bakes it on the spot. Two in the world work. Yours would be the third.

name: Cooling boxes for vaccine transport
description: Boring, essential, governments pay.

name: Robot that cleans solar panels
description: Dust costs solar farms real money. The robot must not fall off.

name: A hot sauce brand
description: Everyone thinks they can do this. Almost everyone is wrong.

name: Frozen meals for old people
description: Enormous market nobody wants to serve because it isn't glamorous.

name: Coffee subscription for offices
description: Offices pay monthly and never cancel. Unglamorous and reliable.

name: A gym with no staff
description: Doors open by phone. Cheaper, colder, weirdly popular.

name: Second-hand children's clothes
description: Kids outgrow everything. Parents feel guilty throwing it out.

name: Non-alcoholic spirits
description: Growing fast, crowded, one brand will win big.

name: Ready meals for dogs
description: Owners spend more on their dog's dinner than their own.

name: A bakery that only sells one thing
description: One product, done perfectly, ten locations.

name: Finding cleaners for holiday flats
description: Everyone with a rental needs this on a Sunday at 4pm.

name: A marketplace for scrap metal
description: Ugly, enormous, and run entirely by phone calls.

name: Booking site for private doctors
description: People pay cash to skip the queue. Uncomfortable but lucrative.

name: Moving company that doesn't lie about the price
description: Fixed quotes. Everyone hates movers.

name: Renting out farm machinery
description: A combine sits unused 340 days a year.

name: A company that just does visas
description: Painful paperwork people gladly pay to avoid.

name: Repair shop chain for phone screens
description: Recession-proof. Boring. Cash every day.

name: Goats that clear overgrown land
description: Cheaper than machines, better for the soil, and people film it.

name: Insurance for wedding photographers
description: One ruined wedding costs €40,000. They all buy it.

name: Professional queue-standers
description: For product launches and government offices. Deeply unfashionable, works everywhere.

name: A company that names other companies
description: You charge €20,000 for a word. Somehow people pay.

name: Renting houseplants to offices
description: They die, you replace them, they pay monthly forever.

name: Cleaning up after crime scenes
description: Nobody wants the job. It pays extremely well.

name: A dating app for one specific hobby
description: Small, obsessive, and they tell everyone.

name: Sperm and egg storage
description: Regulated, expensive, and customers stay for decades.

name: A museum for one very strange thing
description: Tourists will pay €14 to see almost anything.

name: Selling used restaurant equipment
description: Restaurants close constantly. Somebody has to move the fryers.

name: Training pigeons to carry data
description: It works. It is legal. It is very hard to scale.

name: A funeral home for pets
description: Grief has no budget.

name: An app that tells you when to leave a party
description: It went viral for a week. Now what?

name: Fixing bad tattoos
description: An enormous and growing supply of customers.

name: Software for dentists
description: Every practice runs on something dreadful from 2009.

name: A tool that reads planning applications
description: Property developers pay to know before neighbours do.

name: Rota software for hospitals
description: Nurses swap shifts on paper. It costs lives and overtime.

name: Something that finds duplicate charges
description: Companies overpay suppliers constantly. You keep 20%.

name: A search engine for spare parts
description: Factories lose days finding one component.

name: Booking for driving instructors
description: Fragmented, cash-based, entirely unserved.

name: Software that watches your website for you
description: Tells you the checkout broke before customers do.

name: Insurance quotes for weird risks
description: Drone pilots, food trucks, alpaca farms.

name: A tool that writes court filings
description: Lawyers hate it, paralegals love it, courts are wary.

name: Compliance software for small pharmacies
description: Terrifying rules, tiny budgets, no competition.

name: Something that reads energy bills
description: Finds the error. There is always an error.

name: A better system for school reports
description: Teachers spend 40 hours a term on this.

name: Video calls for veterinary clinics
description: Nobody wants to move a sick cat.

name: Fraud checks for online marketplaces
description: Boring, essential, priced per transaction.

name: Route planning for waste collection
description: Councils save millions. Procurement takes forever.

name: A dryer that doesn't destroy clothes
description: Everyone knows it's a problem. Nobody has fixed it.

name: Water sensors for old pipes
description: Utilities lose a third of what they pump.

name: Better packaging for wine shipping
description: Breakage is 4%. That's a fortune.

name: A quiet leaf blower
description: Every town is trying to ban the loud ones.

name: Modular shelving for small flats
description: Cities are shrinking. Furniture hasn't.

name: Cold storage rental by the pallet
description: Small food producers can't afford a warehouse.

name: A better hospital bed
description: Unchanged since 1974, costs $12,000, everybody complains.

name: Air quality monitors for classrooms
description: Parents demand them. Schools have no budget.

name: Bike trailers for tradespeople
description: City vans are dying under congestion charges.

name: Frozen meals for one person
description: Everyone sells for four. A third of homes are one.

name: A tinned fish brand
description: Somehow this became fashionable. Ride it.

name: School uniform resale
description: Parents spend €300 a year on clothes worn 10 months.

name: Cooking sauces from one region
description: Narrow, authentic, exportable.

name: A gym for people over sixty
description: Enormous, growing, embarrassed by normal gyms.

name: Coffee for people who hate coffee
description: A real market nobody addresses seriously.

name: Refill shop for cleaning products
description: Works in three cities. Fails in thirty.

name: A bakery that opens at 4am
description: For nurses, drivers and people coming home.

name: Meal kits for one specific diet
description: Small, obsessive, they never cancel.

name: A company that handles house moves for the elderly
description: Sorting, selling, packing, the difficult conversation.

name: Renting out unused office space by the day
description: Every company has empty desks now.

name: Translation for court hearings
description: Legally required, chronically undersupplied.

name: Finding tradespeople who actually turn up
description: The whole industry is a trust problem.

name: A marketplace for used lab equipment
description: Universities throw away millions.

name: Childcare that opens at 6am
description: For shift workers. Nobody serves them.

name: Storage collection and return
description: People pay to never see the warehouse.

name: Recruitment for one narrow trade
description: Welders, or anaesthetists, or ship engineers.

name: Renting chickens to families
description: Six months, eggs included, most return them.

name: A company that removes wasp nests
description: Seasonal, terrifying, nobody competes on price.

name: Professional apologies
description: Companies outsource the difficult letter.

name: Cleaning solar panels on rooftops
description: Every panel loses 8% a year to dust.

name: A museum of failed products
description: Companies pay to exhibit their disasters.

name: Snow clearing with a subscription
description: You pay all winter whether it snows or not.

name: Renting out a very large aquarium
description: Offices, hotels, dentists. Maintenance is everything.

name: A service that argues with your insurer
description: You take 30% of what they recover.

name: Beekeeping for corporate rooftops
description: Absurd, popular, and the honey is branded.

name: Finding lost pension accounts
description: Billions are unclaimed. You take a percentage.

name: A dating app for one profession
description: Doctors, or farmers, or long-haul pilots.

name: Body doubles for security rehearsals
description: Corporate paranoia is a growth market.

name: Digital estate clearance
description: Someone has to close 200 accounts after a death.

name: A company that tests playground equipment
description: Legally required. Deeply unglamorous.

name: Renting suits by the week
description: For interviews, funerals and court.

name: Satellites that watch shipping
description: Every port, every hour. Governments and hedge funds both want it.

name: An electric motorbike brand
description: Beautiful, expensive, and manufacturing will try to kill you.

name: Lab-grown leather
description: Fashion houses are desperate for it. Nobody has made it feel right.

name: A private members' club
description: Two thousand people paying €4,000 a year to feel chosen.

name: Rockets, but small ones
description: Everyone wants their own satellite now. Very few survive this.

name: An AI that composes film scores
description: Composers hate it. Producers have already signed up.

name: A natural wine label
description: Fashionable, low margin, and everyone thinks they can do it.

name: Drone delivery for hospitals
description: Blood between sites in nine minutes. Regulators move in nine years.

name: A luxury watch brand
description: You need heritage you don't have. Some people build it anyway.

name: A football club in a lower division
description: Absurd economics, enormous emotion, occasional promotion.

name: Sleep tracking that actually works
description: Everyone wants it. The science is thinner than the marketing.

name: A restaurant with one seating a night
description: Twelve covers, one menu, a two-year waiting list.

name: Vertical farms in city centres
description: Photographs beautifully. The electricity bill does not.

name: A talent agency for streamers
description: Twenty percent of very young people's very large incomes.

name: Carbon removal you can verify
description: Buyers are desperate. Proving it is the hard part.

name: A perfume house
description: You are selling a story in a bottle. The bottle costs €3.

name: Robot arms for small factories
description: Everyone under 200 staff wants one and can't afford one.

name: A members' gym with one location
description: Waiting list, no advertising, and it never scales.

name: Hotels in strange buildings
description: Lighthouses, water towers, decommissioned prisons.

name: A fashion brand for one sport
description: Padel, or freediving, or bouldering. Small and obsessive.

name: An AI that reads medical scans
description: Radiologists are stretched thin. Being wrong once ends you.

name: Private aviation, but shared
description: Eight people who each fly six times a year.

name: A record label for one genre
description: You will discover one artist who matters. Probably.

name: Cultured coffee without the bean
description: Climate is killing arabica. Somebody will solve this.

name: A magazine, on paper, in 2026
description: Everyone says it's impossible. A few of them are wrong.

name: Portable toilet rental
description: Festivals, building sites, roadworks. Nobody wants this business. It prints money.

name: Industrial floor cleaning
description: Warehouses, contracts, night shifts. Renewals forever.

name: Medical billing for small clinics
description: Doctors are terrible at this and will pay anyone competent.

name: Scaffolding hire
description: Enormous capital, terrible glamour, extraordinary margins.

name: Uniform supply for restaurants
description: They wear out, they get stained, they reorder every quarter.

name: Pest control
description: Recession-proof, seasonal, and nobody negotiates on price.

name: Car park management
description: Ugly land, automated barriers, cash every single day.

name: Commercial laundry
description: Hotels and hospitals never stop needing this.

name: Gravel and aggregate supply
description: Somebody has to move the stones. It might as well be you.

name: Payroll for care homes
description: Complicated rules, thin margins for them, steady fees for you.

name: Fire extinguisher servicing
description: Legally mandated annual inspection. Nobody ever cancels.

name: Document shredding
description: Regulated destruction of paper. Contracts run for years.

name: Drain unblocking
description: Emergency call-outs at premium rates. Deeply unpleasant.

name: Bookkeeping for tradespeople
description: Plumbers hate paperwork more than they hate paying you.

name: Industrial packaging supply
description: Boxes, tape, pallets. Every business orders monthly.

name: Air conditioning maintenance
description: Installed once, serviced forever, at your price.

name: Insurance claims administration
description: Insurers outsource the tedium. It is very tedious.

name: Sign making
description: Every shop, every office, every building site.

name: Grease trap cleaning for kitchens
description: Legally required. Universally avoided. Reliably lucrative.

name: Mobility equipment rental
description: An ageing population and reliable state reimbursement.

name: Translating technical manuals
description: Machinery ships to 40 countries. Somebody writes those pages.

name: Warehouse racking installation
description: Everyone is building warehouses. Somebody fills them with shelves.

name: Testing electrical equipment
description: Annual, mandatory, per item, forever.

name: Debt collection, done politely
description: The ethical end of an ugly business, and it works better.

name: Livestock feed distribution
description: Farmers buy every month regardless of what the economy does.
